q: What is the deepest point in the ocean?
What is the bottom of the ocean called?
a: The deepest known point in the ocean is the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, located in the western Pacific Ocean. Its depth is approximately 10,994 meters (36,070 feet) below sea level, though measurements vary slightly. To put this in perspective, if Mount Everest were placed at the bottom of the Challenger Deep, its summit would still be more than a mile underwater. The pressure at this depth is over 1,000 times the atmospheric pressure at sea level. Only a handful of people have ever visited the bottom of the Challenger Deep, including Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh in 1960 and filmmaker James Cameron in 2012. The extreme environment supports unique life forms adapted to the darkness, cold, and crushing pressure.

q: What is the tallest mountain on Mars?
What is the biggest mountain on Mars?
a: The tallest mountain on Mars is Olympus Mons, a massive shield volcano that rises about 21.9 kilometers (72,000 feet or 13.6 miles) above the surrounding plain. This makes it nearly three times the height of Mount Everest, which stands at 8,849 meters. Olympus Mons has a base diameter of about 600 kilometers and a caldera that is 80 kilometers wide. It was formed by volcanic activity that built up over a long period, as Mars's lack of plate tectonics allowed lava to erupt repeatedly from the same hotspot. The gentle slopes of Olympus Mons suggest it was built by fluid lava flows rather than explosive eruptions. Its immense size is possible because Mars has lower gravity than Earth.
